object_description: interwoven low base and small-scale three-story volume
design_condition: The extended low base and smaller three-story volume are adapted to the site and create connected outdoor spaces on all sides, but terrain transitions and public circulation remain unresolved.

positive.statement: The volumetric setting is clever and well proportioned, with a scale relevant to school operations.
The clear urban arrangement opens up extensive open spaces on all sides.
The arrangement of school uses and their accesses appears coherent.
The primary-level cluster structures and subdividable class areas offer good conditions for variable teaching methods and varied learning landscapes.
The compactness, moderate spans and linear load transfer positively affect gray energy and greenhouse-gas emissions.
The project has lower construction costs because of its small amount of required space.

negative.statement: The open-space designs lack a comprehensible idea, and the chosen formal means do not adequately counteract the solitary building.
Terrain modeling and level transitions at the entrances are neither functionally nor design-wise resolved.
The proposed networking and thoroughfares guarantee only limited, obstacle-free access.
The basic level's separate access and outdoor space are not fully implemented, causing conflicts with the public area.
The deep floor plans create rear dark zones, and not all areas benefit equally from daylight.
The basic level only partially meets requirements for spatial organization, classroom outdoor connections and daylight.
The primary level's daylight, visual references and access dimensions are questioned, while the dense ground-floor structure fails to create the desired qualities.
The caretaker's apartment in the school entrance area seems strange.
Limited insulation values and additional construction complexity tend to worsen the gray-energy balance.
